styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Castle, Royal Mile and the Old Town closes.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Arthur's Seat, Calton Hill and the coast.

stays.why: Walk to the Castle, Royal Mile and Grassmarket. Lively and central, but hilly and noisy at night.
Georgian streets, Princes Street shops and gardens. Quieter, flatter and close to Waverley station.
Waterfront bars and restaurants, cheaper rooms. Trams and buses reach the centre in about 20 minutes.
Near the station, airport tram and bus links. Good value and a short walk to the West End.

food: Try Scottish classics: haggis, neeps and tatties, Cullen skink soup and a full Scottish breakfast.
Look for a pub lunch in the Old Town or Stockbridge; expect roughly GBP 12–20 for a main.
Seafood is good in Leith: check the day's catch and book ahead for dinner.
Cheap eats: pies, baked potatoes and sandwiches for about GBP 5–9; many museums have cafés.
Book dinner ahead in August, when festival crowds fill central restaurants.
more_time: Swap a city afternoon for a climb up Arthur's Seat: a rough walk of about 1–1.5 hours up and down; wear grippy shoes.
Take a train or bus to South Queensferry to see the Forth Bridges, or a boat trip to Inchcolm Abbey; check sailings on the day.
History fans can add a day trip to Stirling Castle or Rosslyn Chapel; times and tickets vary, so check on the day.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the Castle, Royal Mile and a museum or two, with time for Arthur's Seat or Leith.

month_notes: Cold and often wet: highs near 6°C, lows near 2°C, rain on about 14 days. Pack a warm waterproof coat.
Still cold: highs around 7°C, rain on about 13 days. Short daylight; plan indoor sights.
Cool and wet: highs near 9°C, rain on about 16 days. Good museum weather.
Milder: highs near 11°C, rain on about 12 days. Pleasant for walking the Royal Mile.
Spring warmth: highs near 14°C, rain on about 13 days. Good for Arthur's Seat.
Long days: highs near 17°C, rain on about 14 days. Evenings stay light late.
Warmest month: highs near 18°C, rain on about 17 days. Busy festival season; book early.
Warm and busy: highs near 18°C, rain on about 15 days. Festival crowds and higher prices.
Cooling: highs near 16°C, rain on about 13 days. Quieter than August, still good for walks.
Autumn: highs near 13°C, rain on about 15 days. Bring layers and a rain jacket.
Cold and damp: highs near 9°C, rain on about 14 days. Dark early; indoor sights shine.
Coldest feel: highs near 7°C, rain on about 16 days. Short days and festive lights in the centre.

climate_guide.summary: Cool and changeable: mild summers, cold winters and rain in every month. Rarely very hot or very cold.

items.title: Rain any month
items.text: Expect rain on roughly 12–17 days each month. Showers pass quickly; carry a light waterproof.

items.title: Mild summers
items.text: July and August highs sit near 18°C, lows near 12°C. Rarely hot; layers help.

items.title: Cold winters
items.text: January highs near 6°C, lows near 2°C. Wind off the sea makes it feel colder; bring a warm coat.

items.title: Windy and exposed
items.text: Hills and the coast are breezier. A windproof layer matters more than an umbrella.

items.title: Long summer days
items.text: June and July give very long daylight, so late walks are easy. Winter days are short.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Waterproof jacket, layers, comfortable walking shoes for cobbles and hills, and a warm hat in winter.

transit.best: Walk the centre; use buses and trams for Leith, the airport and longer hops.

modes.text: Trams link the airport, Haymarket, Princes Street, Waverley and Leith. Buy tickets at stop machines.
Lothian buses cover the city. Pay with exact cash or contactless; day and multi-day tickets available.
Metered taxis are plentiful. Uber and Bolt also operate in Edinburgh.
Not worth it in the centre: many streets are closed and parking is scarce and pricey.
The centre is very walkable, though hilly with cobbles. Bikes and e-bikes are easy to hire, with some cycle lanes.
Airlink 100 runs 24 hours to Waverley Bridge, about 20–30 minutes.
